title: Generalizability of Gottman and Colleagues' Affective Process Models of Couples' Relationship Outcomes
author: Hyoun K. Kim; Deborah M. Capaldi; Lynn Crosby (Oregon Social Learning Center, Eugene)
accessedVia: curl GET of the PMC article page, then local HTML-to-text extraction (tags stripped, paragraph order preserved). The WebFetch summarizing model declined verbatim reproduction, so text was extracted locally instead.
notes: THE HIGHEST-VALUE ARTIFACT IN THIS CAPTURE: an independent (non-Gottman-affiliated) attempted replication that FAILED. PMCID PMC1828692, PMID 17372624, NIHMSID NIHMS13632, DOI 10.1111/j.1741-3737.2006.00343.x. Free-to-read NIH-funded AUTHOR MANUSCRIPT deposited in PMC; the publisher's final edited version is paywalled. This is NOT a CC-BY license - treat as free-to-read, not freely redistributable. Body text captured from 'Abstract' through the end of the Discussion; the trailing Acknowledgments (grant boilerplate) and author contact/fax lines were stripped, as were PMC UI artifacts ('Open in a new tab'). Author sentences are byte-verbatim and in original order. In-text reference markers appear as plain author-year text because the source HTML wrapped them in links. Statistical tables appear inline where the source placed them. NOTE ON SCOPE (load-bearing): this paper tests Gottman et al. (1998)'s affective PROCESS models, and the authors state explicitly that they did NOT test the discriminant function models, the contingent positive affect path model, or the physiological soothing model. It is therefore a generalizability/replication failure of the process models, not a head-on test of the four-horsemen divorce-prediction equation.
